stem:
Rohan knows $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$ with correspondence $A \leftrightarrow D$, $B \leftrightarrow E$, $C \leftrightarrow F$. Side $AB$ equals side $DE$, and $\angle BAC$ equals $\angle EDF$.

Which claim correctly uses the congruence?

options.text: Side $BC$ equals side $EF$, as corresponding sides under $A \leftrightarrow D$, $B \leftrightarrow E$, $C \leftrightarrow F$.
Congruence of the triangles is enough even if the vertex matching is ignored.
Only sides can be equal from congruence; angles need a separate rule.

teacher.key_rationale: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal under the given matching, so BC corresponds to EF. Angle at B matches angle at E, not F. Vertex order matters. Angles are included.
